title: OLTP vs OLAP: Why Data Models Matter

scenes.line1: Why do OLTP and OLAP need
scenes.say: Ever wonder why databases for transactions and analytics look so different? Let’s break down why the data model matters.

scenes.label: OLTP
scenes.sub: Handles fast inserts, updates, and deletes
scenes.say: OLTP systems are built for speed and reliability. Think banking apps—lots of quick updates, and data must stay consistent.

scenes.label: OLAP
scenes.sub: Optimized for big queries and reporting
scenes.say: OLAP systems, on the other hand, are all about crunching huge datasets for analysis and reporting. They’re built for complex questions, not quick edits.
OLTP uses normalized tables to reduce redundancy and keep data clean. OLAP uses dimensional models—facts and dimensions—often denormalized for fast queries.
In OLAP, facts are the numbers you measure, dimensions are the details you slice by, and grain is the level of detail for each record.

scenes.question: Should OLAP always be normalized?
scenes.right: No—OLAP denormalizes for performance. Normalization is key for OLTP.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for this: OLAP systems usually denormalize to make queries faster. Normalization is great for OLTP, but not for analytics.
